rationale: MIN of a stock (che) and a flow (capx) is dimensionally incoherent and, because cash typically exceeds one year of capex for most firms, the conditioner will collapse to capx/ppegt — a renewal-intensity leg already tested in Backlog-Addressing Renewal Value and Demand-Triggered Investment Value — so it does not actually measure the "cash-covered" mechanism claimed.

Charging current capex against cash before scaling by installed capital is a substantive (not cosmetic) reformulation of the archive's strongest leg che/(che+ppent), since a material fraction of firms have capx comparable to or exceeding cash and will flip to negative net optionality, giving the signal a genuinely different cross-section.

A coherent weakest-link combination of two independently validated legs with distinct denominators and a defensible motivation (screening out passively asset-light firms), though it is incremental relative to the several existing MIN-composites and will lose coverage through emp.

Because implied retirement (capx − Δppegt) is typically an order of magnitude smaller than oancf, the MIN will almost always select the recycling term, so the expression silently discards the cash-flow-yield component the hypothesis relies on and reduces to a retirement-to-market-cap ranking dominated by gross-PP&E reconciliation noise.

Pairing asset rejuvenation with labor-productivity trend is economically sensible and avoids the shared-denominator artifact of Productive Renewal Value, but it is a modest recombination of two already-tested legs rather than a new mechanism.

This is an explicit MIN→MUL operator swap on Payoff-Validated Capital Optionality with identical economic inputs, i.e. exactly the cosmetic variant the research objective warns against, and the product of two percentile ranks will be highly correlated with their minimum.
